_description: Cross-language verse-numbering alignment between the Armenian (Nor Ejmiatsin) corpus and English (NKJV/KJVAIC via API.Bible). Consumed by hub/services/verse_mapping.py. Distinct from hub/data/bible_hy/errata.json, which corrects Armenian *scrape* fidelity against the Armenian source itself -- this file aligns Armenian versification against English versification.

_kinds.relocation: A sub-range of a reading lives at a different chapter/book location in `language`. `mode: whole_range` remaps the entire triggered range 1:1 to a different book/chapter (e.g. Esther's Greek additions -> ESG). `mode: tail_split` keeps everything up to `split_after` in place and relocates only the tail past it (e.g. the Romans doxology).
_kinds.composite: Verses of `usfm` are embedded inside another book's chapter in `language` only (not standalone there). The embedding is resolved offline, once, by a corpus-derivation script (see scripts/derive_azariah_hy.py) -- at runtime this rule only reports a `gap` when a request touches verses the two languages don't reconcile on, instead of silently under-returning.
_kinds.no_equivalent: Verses exist in the OTHER language with no counterpart in `language` at all. Requests get truncated to `truncate_to`, and the excluded tail is reported as a gap rather than silently dropped.

rules.note: Armenian numbers the closing doxology as Romans 14:24-26; NKJV ends chapter 14 at verse 23 and places the same doxology at 16:25-27.

KJVAIC stores the Greek Esther additions as standalone ESG 1-7; the liturgical source refers to the first addition as Esther 10:4-13, which maps to ESG 1:4-13. Armenian keeps the additions as native Esther chapters 10-16 (Vulgate arrangement), so no 'hy' rule is needed.

gap.note: KJV/KJVAIC splits a doxology verse the Armenian keeps whole; exact split point unconfirmed (live API.Bible access blocked until 2026-08-04 -- see PR #465).
